title: Chapter 2 Quiz — Hamiltonian Paths and Cycles

questions.question: If $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle and removing a vertex subset $S$ of size $4$ disconnects $G$, what is the maximum possible number of connected components in $G - S$?
questions.explanation: Deleting $|S|$ vertices from a Hamiltonian cycle breaks the cycle into at most $|S| = 4$ arcs covering every remaining vertex, so $G - S$ has at most $4$ components.

questions.question: In Pósa's proof that no closed knight's tour exists on a $4 \times n$ board, what contradicts the forced alternation between outer rows ($1, 4$) and inner rows ($2, 3$)?

options.text: The outer rows have more squares than the inner rows
Every outer square would have to share the same chessboard color, yet outer rows have both colors
Corners have degree 1 on a 4 x n board
A knight cannot move between rows 2 and 3

questions.explanation: Since a knight on an outer row must land on an inner row and both have $2n$ squares, the tour alternates outer-inner. Because knight moves also flip chessboard color, all $2n$ outer squares would share one color.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of edges that guarantees a simple graph on $n = 8$ vertices has a Hamiltonian cycle?
questions.explanation: Any graph on $n \ge 3$ vertices with $\binom{n-1}{2} + 2 = 23$ edges satisfies Ore's theorem; $K_7$ plus one pendant edge has $22$ edges and no Hamiltonian cycle.

questions.question: Which of the following standard graphs does NOT have a Hamiltonian cycle?
questions.explanation: The Petersen graph has a Hamiltonian path, but no Hamiltonian cycle. $Q_4$, $P_3 \times P_4$ ($3\cdot 4$ even), and $K_{5,5}$ are all Hamiltonian.
